correctness.rationale: The rotation/polar-vertex geometry gives correct sector support functions in both residue branches. Inverting the strictly monotone ratio proves CDF and density; exact A,B,C integrations and factorization give unique least-squares minimizer and positive residual. Endpoint witnesses plus monotonic support error prove the unique Hausdorff optimum. Uniform angle folding gives the weak uniform limit and controlled Taylor remainders. Direct independent polygon-vertex quadrature, CDF and asymptotic tests in the included script passed for the specified finite list. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The old zero-vs-nonzero Radon parity is explicitly credited to Heil and Mandal–Sain–Paul. The new assertion consists of the all-angle quantitative distribution, uniform defect limit, exact L2 and Hausdorff optimal scales, and sharp asymptotic coefficients for N divisible by four. Inspected full primary texts and indexed related claims neither state these results nor imply them without a new angular-sector integration, distribution inversion and metric optimization. Uninspected classical/older full texts are a real but not decisive remaining priority risk.

value.rationale: The new quantitative polar-projection defect is intrinsic to the planar exceptions of a major convex-geometric rigidity problem. It determines a full angular distribution and its universal scaling law, and solves both canonical best-homothety metrics with distinct optimizers and sharp rates. This is a natural exact benchmark for geometric near-rigidity rather than a trivial rephrasing of the already-known polygon parity or a numerical table; no downstream all-convex-bodies theorem is claimed.
